## What it is

Draft Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) with Supplemental Information for Troy School District, a school district in the State of Michigan, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, presented to the Board of Education on October 4, 2022. The transmittal letter is signed by Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, and Kandice Moynihan, Director of Finance, Business Services, at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098-4777. Plante & Moran, appointed by the Troy Board of Education for the 2021-22 fiscal year, issued an unmodified opinion dated October 4, 2022; there were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards. ASBO International has awarded the district a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years ended June 30, 1989-2021.

## Officials

Board of Education: Karl Schmidt (President), Dr. Nicole Wilson (Vice President), Gary Hauff (Secretary), and Trustees Vital Anne, Steve Gottlieb, Elizabeth Hammond, and Dr. Nancy Philippart. Administration: Superintendent Richard Machesky, Ed.D.; Assistant Superintendents Rick West, Christine DiPilato, Jordan Harris, and Kristine Griffor; Kerry Birmingham, Director of Communications and Strategic Initiatives.

The audited statement of net position reports a deficit of $(178,223,715) and a change in net position of $22,834,243, which management attributes primarily to the net decrease in deferred pension and OPEB costs. Statement of activities expenses total $187,017,923 against charges for services of $4,858,412 and operating grants of $60,219,352.

## Fund results

| Fund | Ending balance |
| --- | --- |
| General Fund | $32,980,837 |
| 2019 Capital Projects Fund | $6,840,122 |
| Nonmajor governmental funds | $10,833,127 |
| Total governmental funds | $50,654,086 |

Governmental fund revenue was $210,994,466 and expenditures $220,115,078, for a net change in fund balances of $(7,190,292). MD&A reports the combined fund balance decreased $7.2 million, the General Fund rose $0.2 million to $33.0 million (a seventh consecutive annual increase, with unassigned balance at 16.6 percent of 2022 general operating expenditures), special revenue funds went from $3.1 million to $5.9 million, debt service funds rose $1.1 million, and capital project funds fell $11.3 million. Sinking fund millage collections were $4.2 million.

## Debt and capital

General obligation bonds outstanding fell to $116,165,000 from $130,280,000, with unamortized premium of $6,970,844. Total long-term debt ended at $131,831,910, with $17,430,446 due within one year. The rating is AA/Stable, affirmed by Standard & Poor's in May 2021; unqualified general obligation debt of $12.0 million sits below the $647.9 million statutory limit, and qualified debt totals $104.2 million. Net capital assets were $198,957,764, with additions of $7.8 million for building renovations, site work, and bus purchases.

## Outlook

The 2022-2023 foundation allowance rises $450 per pupil to $9,880. Spring 2022 enrollment was 12,519 students, approximately 600 fewer than the district was funded for in 2020, or roughly $6 million less annual operational revenue. Approximately 65.5 percent of General Fund revenue comes from the foundation allowance and state sources.

**Report identity and audit opinion.** Troy School District issued its Annual Comprehensive Financial Report with Supplemental Information for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022; the version placed before the Board of Education on October 4, 2022 carries "Draft" markings on its supplemental and statistical pages. The transmittal letter, dated October 4, 2022 and addressed to the Citizens of Troy and the Board Members, is signed by Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, and Kandice Moynihan, Director of Finance, Business Services, at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098-4777 (248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013, rwest@troy.k12.mi.us). Plante & Moran, appointed by the Troy Board of Education for the 2021-22 fiscal year, rendered an unmodified opinion on the governmental activities, each major fund, and the aggregate remaining fund information; its separate Government Auditing Standards report is also dated October 4, 2022, and there were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards. ASBO International has awarded a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years ended June 30, 1989-2021, the certificate signed by President William A. Sutter and Executive Director David J. Lewis. The district has no component units.

**Officials.** Board of Education: Karl Schmidt (President), Dr. Nicole Wilson (Vice President), Gary Hauff (Secretary), and Trustees Vital Anne, Steve Gottlieb, Elizabeth Hammond, and Dr. Nancy Philippart. Administration: Richard Machesky, Ed.D. (Superintendent), Rick West (Business Services), Christine DiPilato (Secondary Instruction), Jordan Harris (Employee Services), Kristine Griffor (Elementary Instruction), and Kerry Birmingham (Director of Communications and Strategic Initiatives).

**District profile.** The district operates twelve elementary schools, four middle schools, two traditional and one non-traditional high school, and the East campus of the International Academy, located 20 minutes north of Detroit in suburban Oakland County. Troy covers just over 26.61 square miles, is the largest city in Oakland County and the 13th largest in Michigan, with a population of approximately 80,000, more than 6,000 businesses with a market value over $12 billion, and more than 57% of residents holding a bachelor's degree or higher. Thirteen schools have received the National Blue Ribbon Award: Barnard, Bemis, Leonard, Martell, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass, Wattles, Larson, Boulan Park, Athens, Troy High, and the International Academy. The building inventory totals 448.74 acres and 2,185,181 square feet serving 12,519 students, with 128.30 acres of vacant property; Troy High School occupies 73.13 acres and 343,207 square feet (built 1992, 2,101 students) and Athens High School 50.00 acres and 398,426 square feet (1974, 1,554 students), while Troy Union Elementary, built in 1925, is the oldest building. The 2026 Strategic Plan, approved by board resolution, succeeded the World Class 2020 vision introduced in 2015-16; the district participates in the BELE Network and hired a Supervisor of Equity, Inclusion, and Community Relationships in 2020-2021.

**Economic condition and outlook.** The 2022-2023 state budget raises every Michigan district's per-pupil foundation allowance by $450, producing a $9,880 foundation allowance for Troy. Enrollment as of Spring 2022 was 12,519 students, approximately 600 fewer than the district received funding for in 2020, equating to approximately $6 million less annual operational revenue. Approximately 65.5 percent of total General Fund revenue comes from the foundation allowance and state sources, and labor market pressure has raised wage rates in custodial, food service, transportation, and special education support. On November 8, 2022, voters will consider a $555 million bond proposal for district-wide infrastructure upgrades; the last approved bond was in 2013, its funds expected to be exhausted in the next fiscal year, and passage is expected to raise the debt millage by 2.0 mills.

**Government-wide statements.** Net position (deficit) at June 30, 2022 was $(178,223,715), against $(201,057,958) at the beginning of the year, for a change in net position of $22,834,243 that MD&A attributes primarily to the net decrease in deferred pension and OPEB costs. Total assets were $275,756,255, including cash and cash equivalents of $35,230,239, other receivables of $561,076, due from other governmental units of $26,944,685, restricted assets of $13,129,507, and net capital assets of $195,481,875 plus $3,475,889 not being depreciated. Deferred outflows totaled $65,093,678: bond refunding charges $414,288, pension costs $46,666,056, OPEB costs $18,013,334. Total liabilities were $382,908,130, including accounts payable $3,190,370, due to other governmental units $3,798,115, accrued salaries and wages $9,503,772, accrued payroll taxes and fringe benefits $6,664,114, accrued interest payable $552,804, unearned revenue $2,988,034, noncurrent liabilities of $17,430,446 due within one year and $114,401,464 thereafter, net pension liability $210,869,230, and net OPEB liability $13,509,781. Deferred inflows of $136,165,518 comprise revenue in support of pension contributions made after the measurement date $13,922,709, deferred pension cost reductions $70,825,415, and deferred OPEB cost reductions $51,417,394. Net position components: net investment in capital assets $82,106,682; restricted for capital projects $3,333,800, food service $2,048,648, and debt service $917,494; unrestricted $(266,630,339).

The statement of activities reports total expenses of $187,017,923 — instruction $102,842,242, support services $67,319,848, athletics $2,222,512, food services $4,355,229, community services $7,238,912, interest $3,036,029, other debt costs $3,151 — offset by charges for services of $4,858,412 and operating grants of $60,219,352, for net expense of $(121,940,159). General revenue of $144,774,402 comprises property taxes levied for general purposes $35,621,090, debt service $17,683,639, and capital projects $4,214,109; unrestricted state aid $82,313,714; unrestricted federal grants $47,907; interest and investment earnings $112,766; net gain on sale and disposal of capital assets $1,122,207; student activities $2,866,759; and other $792,211.

**Governmental funds.** Combined fund balance was $50,654,086: General Fund $32,980,837, 2019 Capital Projects Fund $6,840,122, nonmajor funds $10,833,127. Fund revenue totaled $210,994,466 (local $66,148,986, state $113,606,709, federal $21,112,713, interdistrict $10,126,058) and expenditures $220,115,078 (instruction $115,847,916, support services $58,900,439, athletics $2,188,989, food services $4,293,308, community services $4,339,915, principal $14,115,000, interest $3,801,552, capital outlay $16,624,808), leaving expenditures over revenue of $(9,120,612); other financing sources of $1,930,320 produced a net change of $(7,190,292) from a beginning balance of $57,844,378. General Fund unassigned balance was $28,736,352 with $3,361,479 assigned to the subsequent year's budget. MD&A reports the General Fund rose $0.2 million to $33.0 million in a seventh consecutive year of additions, with unassigned balance at 16.6 percent of 2022 general operating expenditures against a policy minimum of 15 percent; special revenue fund balance rose from $3.1 million to $5.9 million (Food Service up $1.8 million, Community Service up $0.7 million, Preschool up $0.5 million on federal childcare stabilization grants); debt service funds rose $1.1 million; capital project funds fell $11.3 million on 2019 bond construction; sinking fund millage collections were $4.2 million.

Budgetary comparison for the General Fund: total revenue original budget $163,603,984, final $170,565,175, actual $170,116,893, variance $(448,282); total expenditures original $166,301,381, final $173,657,294, actual $172,507,660, variance $(1,149,634); net change in fund balance actual $246,735 versus a final budget of $(454,619); ending fund balance $32,980,837 against a final budget of $32,279,483. The final amendment was adopted in June 2022; budgeted revenue had been increased $7.0 million and federal revenue $5.0 million (ESSER III and Section 11t under the American Rescue Plan), with Sections 31o and 147c categorical increases and $1.2 million of transfers in from the Community Service and Troy Preschool Funds.

**Capital assets and debt.** Capital assets totaled $400,750,723 less accumulated depreciation and amortization of $201,792,959, for net $198,957,764 (2021: $392,912,216, $193,697,815, and $199,214,401). Components: land $1,861,010, construction in progress $1,614,879, buildings and improvements $345,755,277, furniture and equipment $50,989,269, lease asset - building $530,288. Additions of $7.8 million covered building renovations, site work, and bus purchases; the year's net change was a decrease of approximately $0.3 million. Depreciation and amortization of $9,725,109 was charged to support services $5,734,528, community services $3,529,994, instruction $242,690, athletics $169,880, and food services $48,017. Construction commitments totaled $8,090,089 spent to date and $8,836,206 remaining, split between the 2019 Capital Projects Fund ($4,089,597 and $6,349,512) and the Sinking Fund ($4,000,492 and $2,486,694).

Long-term debt moved from $145,880,806 to $131,831,910, with $17,430,446 due within one year. General obligation bonds ended at $116,165,000 (from $130,280,000, reductions of $14,115,000) with unamortized premium of $6,970,844; leases $422,874; compensated absences $8,048,192; other termination benefits $225,000. Debt service to maturity is $116,165,000 principal plus $21,651,596 interest, $137,816,596 total, with $19,281,825 payable in 2023. Outstanding series: $52,710,000 2014 GO bond ($2,000,000 remaining, 5.00%, maturing May 1, 2023); $31,930,000 2015 refunding ($12,930,000, 5.00%, May 1, 2026); $40,000,000 2016 GO ($31,800,000, 2.94%-4.50%, May 1, 2032); $7,125,000 2018 GO ($6,610,000, 3.00%-3.75%, May 1, 2040); $22,630,000 2019 GO ($19,175,000, 5.00%, May 1, 2034); $6,100,000 2020 GO ($5,390,000, 2.00%, May 1, 2035); $7,110,000 2021 refunding ($4,945,000, 0.30%, May 1, 2023); and $33,315,000 2021 refunding ($33,315,000, 0.30%-1.56%, May 1, 2028). Standard & Poor's affirmed an AA/Stable rating in May 2021; unqualified general obligation debt of $12.0 million is well below the $647.9 million statutory limit, and qualified debt totals $104.2 million. The Troy Career Center building lease has $422,874 principal and $42,854 interest remaining, $465,728 in total.

**MPSERS pension and OPEB.** Required and actual pension contributions were $31,043,947, including a $13,922,709 allocation of state revenue funding the MPSERS UAAL stabilization rate; OPEB contributions were $7,221,409. Pension expense was $25,126,063 and the district recognized OPEB recovery of $7,228,236. Net pension liability of $210,869,230 and net OPEB liability of $13,509,781 were measured as of September 30, 2021 from a September 30, 2020 valuation rolled forward; proportions were approximately 0.89 and 0.90 percent, changes of (0.69) percent for pension and (1.40) percent for OPEB. Plan fiduciary net position was 72.32 percent of total pension liability and 88.87 percent of total OPEB liability. Discount rates were 6.00 to 6.80 percent (pension) and 6.95 percent (OPEB); a one-point lower pension discount rate would put the liability at $301,485,812 and a one-point higher rate at $135,742,141. Statutorily required FY2022 contributions were $30,532,065 for pension (36.50 percent of covered payroll of $83,641,260) and $6,816,094 for OPEB (8.15 percent). Payables to the plans at June 30, 2022 were $6,200,116 and $971,051.

**Other notes.** The district designated 11 financial institutions and used 2; $41,417,368 of bank deposits were uninsured and uncollateralized. MILAF holdings were $55,838 (Cash Management) and $7,890,866 (MAX Class), both rated AAAm by S&P. Restricted assets comprise unspent bond proceeds and interest $7,946,704, unspent sinking fund taxes $3,712,505, and unspent debt service taxes $1,470,298. Unearned revenue of $2,988,034 covers categorical aid $2,161,211, tuition and fees $519,536, student lunch accounts $192,331, and property taxes $114,956. Transfers of $400,000 from the Preschool Fund and $800,000 from the Community Service Fund went to the General Fund, and $8,411 moved from the Capital Maintenance Fund to the Facility Rentals Fund. Industrial facilities tax exemptions under PA 198 of 1974 and brownfield redevelopment agreements reduced property tax revenue by $126,000, with approximately $108,000 reimbursed by the State. Insurance is commercial with participation in the SET-SEG shared risk program. GASB Statement No. 87 was adopted July 1, 2021 with no effect on net position; GASB 96 applies for June 30, 2023 and GASB 101 for June 30, 2025. Custodial funds held $113,422 of cash with net position of $104,643.

**Statistical section.** For tax year 2021 / fiscal 2022, taxable value was $4,319,004,145 (residential $2,724,884,777, commercial $861,201,980, industrial $237,006,200, personal property $495,911,188) at a total rate of 26.4658 mills, with estimated actual value of $8,638,008,290. District millages for 2021 were homestead 3.3878, non-homestead 18.0000, debt 4.1000, and sinking fund 0.9780, alongside overlapping levies of 4.0132 (County), 1.5057 (community college), 3.2012 (intermediate school district), 6.0000 (State Education), and 10.0154 (City of Troy). The $57,806,243 levy was 98.37 percent currently collected and 99.50 percent collected including $654,758 of delinquent collections. The largest taxpayer was Somerset Collections at $49,518,400 taxable value (0.92%), followed by DTE at $36,077,230. Net general bonded debt was $121,665,547, 2.82 percent of taxable value and $1,401 per capita; total direct and overlapping debt was $144,183,395, including $12,176,370 (City of Troy), $14,585,276 (Oakland County), and $2,727,048 (Oakland ISD). The legal debt margin was $635,850,622 with net debt subject to limit of $12,000,000, or 1.85 percent. Population was 86,836, per capita personal income $49,211, and unemployment 2.10 percent; the largest employers were William Beaumont Hospital (2,300 employees, 5.34%) and Troy School District (1,308, 3.03%). Full-time equivalent staff totaled 1,072 (instruction 891, support services 164, community service 15, athletics 1, food service 1). Operating indicators: enrollment 12,519, operating expenditures $172,507,660, cost per pupil $13,780, operating revenue $170,116,893, revenue per pupil $13,589, 850 teaching staff, 11.00 percent qualifying for free or reduced meals, average teacher salary $76,031, and 74 buses. Building counts and February-count enrollment: one early childhood building (72,000 square feet, 197), twelve elementary (717,462 square feet, 5,047), four middle (450,492 square feet, 2,812), and four high schools (851,426 square feet, 4,463).
